IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SUBHASH UPADHYAY
Writ Petition (S/B) No.83 of 2025
Jagdish Chandra Purohit -----Petitioner
Versus
Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Uttarakhand University
and Others
----Respondents
--------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Piyush Garg, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. Shakti
Sourabh Purohit, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for respondent nos.1 and 2.
Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior Counsel assisted by Mr. C.S.
Dalakoti, learned counsel for respondent no.3.
--------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Subhash Upadhyay J.)
1. The present writ petition has been filed for the
following reliefs:
"(i) To issue a writ order or direction in the nature of
Certiorari for quashing recommendations/proceedings
of the selection committee dated 16.02.2024, by
means of which the name of respondent no. 2 has
been forwarded/recommended by the committee for
appointment on the post of Assistant Professor
(Statistics) under EWS category and for quashing of
the minutes of meeting of the Board of Management
dated 09.08.2024 by means of which the Managing
Council has approved the recommendation of the
Selection Committee.
(ii) To issue a writ, order or direction in the nature of
mandamus directing the respondents to recommend
1

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
and give appointment to the petitioner on the post of
Assistant Professor (EWS category) in College of
Forestry, Rani-Chauri, Tehri, Garhwal, VCSG,
Uttarakhand, University of Horticulture and Forestry,
Bharsar, Pauri Garhwal, in pursuance of the
Advertisement Notice No. UUHf/dt/f.no.01/01 of
2023, dated 14.08.2023.
(iii) To pass any other suitable order which this
Hon'ble Court may deem fit and proper in the facts
and circumstances of the present case."
2. The petitioner who belongs to the
economically weaker section (EWS) applied for the post
of Assistant Professor (Statistics) in the College of
Forestry, Veer Chandra Singh Garhwali Uttarakhand
University of Horticulture and Forestry (hereinafter
referred to as "VCSG University").
3. As per the advertisement issued on
14.08.2023, amongst various posts advertised for
different streams one post of Assistant Professor
(Statistics) in the College of Forestry was reserved for
EWS category.
4. The controversy in the present case relates to
the non-selection of the petitioner, who belongs to the
EWS category, to the post of Assistant Professor
(Statistics) under the said category.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner contended
that against the post of Assistant Professor (Statistics)
to be filled up under the EWS category three candidates
2

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
applied and only two candidates i.e. the petitioner and
respondent no.3 were short-listed for interview.
6. It is further case of the petitioner that as
respondent no.3 does not belong to the EWS category,
as such, he was wrongly included in the panel and his
selection and recommendation against the post
earmarked for EWS category is against the Uttarakhand
Public Services (Reservation for Economically Weaker
Sections) Act, 2019 (hereinafter referred to as "Act of
2019"). He thus submits that the said recommendation
made in favour of respondent no.3 being against the
provisions of the Act is liable to be struck down.
7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent
no.1 and 2 submits that respondent no.3 was found to
be more meritorious and was selected and
recommended for appointment as Assistant Professor
(Statistics) but as he could not submit his EWS
Certificate as per the prescribed format, as such, no
appointment order has been issued in his favour. It has
further been contended that as the name of the
petitioner was not recommended by the Selection
Committee, hence, the petitioner has no right to claim
appointment.
3

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
8. Learned Senior Counsel for respondent no.3
submitted that the respondent no.3 had not applied for
the post of Assistant Professor (Statistics) under the
EWS category and had applied as an unreserved
candidate. It is submitted that an unreserved category
candidate can also apply for the post of Assistant
Professor under the EWS category. Learned Senior
Counsel submits that, as per Sub-section 3 of Section 3
of the Act of 2019, if any vacancy reserved for EWS
category cannot be filled up due to non-availability of a
suitable candidate then such vacancy can be filled up
from suitable general category candidates. He thus,
submits that, as petitioner was lower in merit, as such,
Selection Committee rightly recommended the case of
respondent no.3 for appointment as Assistant Professor.
9. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
10. A perusal of the record reveals that the
petitioner sought certain information under the Right to
Information Act and the information with regard to the
proceedings of the Selection Committee and the marks
which were awarded to respondent no.3 were provided
to the petitioner. The recommendation made by the
Selection Committee in favour of respondent no.3 and
4

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
the marks obtained by him is enclosed as Annexure
No.3 to the writ petition, which reads as under:
"PROCEEDINGS OF THE SELECTION COMMITTEE
The meeting of Selection Committee for the Post of
Assistant Professor (Statistics) under EWS category
held on 16.02.2024 at The Competent Palace Hotel
Chakrata Road, Selaqui Industrial Area, Central Hope
Town, Selaqui, Dehradun (Uttarakhand) from 10:30
am onwards. Total ....02... candidates were called for
interview and two appeared for interview.
On the basis of presentation and performance in the
interview the committee recommends the name of the
following candidate for appointment to the post:
S.No. Name Sr. No in
the
Score Canal
Marks
(Max Marks
25)
1. Pankaj
Bahuguna S/o
Sri Prabhakar
Dutt Bahuguna
2 21
11. This Court, on the basis of the submissions
made by learned counsel for the parties, passed an
order on 17.08.2026 asking the university to disclose
the criteria, if any, fixed by it for adjudging suitability of
candidate during interview and also place on record the
5

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
marks obtained by the petitioner. The order dated
17.08.2026 passed by the Court reads as under:
"1. Mr. Piyush Garg and Mr. Shakti Saurabh Purohit,
learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. C.K. Sharma, learned counsel for respondent
nos.1 and 2. 3. Mr. C.D. Bahuguna, learned Senior
Counsel assisted by Mr. C.S. Dalakoti, learned counsel
for respondent no.3.
4. The post of Assistant Professor (Statistics) was
advertised showing it to be reserved for Economically
Weaker Sections category (EWS category). The
petitioner is EWS category candidate and after short-listing, he participated in the interview along with
respondent no.3, who, admittedly, does not belong to
EWS category. However, respondent no.3 was
recommended for appointment against the vacancy in
question.
5. In the counter-affidavit filed by the University, it is
admitted that respondent no.3 does not belong to
EWS category and it is stated that consequently, he
has not been given appointment.
6. Respondent no.3 has filed a counter-affidavit and
has placed reliance on Section 3(3) of the
Uttarakhand Public Services (Reservation for
Economically Weaker Sections) Act, 2019, which is as
follows:-
"3(3) If, in any recruitment year any vacancy
reserved for Economically Weaker Section cannot be
filled up due to nonavailability of a suitable candidate,
then such vacancies for that particular recruitment
year shall not be carried forward to the next
recruitment year as backlog and such vacancy shall
be filled up from a suitable candidate belonging to
General category."
7. As per own case of respondent no.3, he could be
recommended for appointment against the vacancy
reserved for EWS category only if the petitioner had
been adjudged as nonsuitable for the post in question.
8. In the counter-affidavit filed by the University, it
has not disclosed the criteria prescribed for adjudging
the suitability of the candidate during interview, nor
has brought on record the marks obtained by the
petitioner. It is stated that the marks obtained by
candidates have been kept in a sealed cover and, in
case, this Court would direct, the same shall be
produced before it. Respondent no.3 has obtained 21
marks out 25 in the interview. However, marks of the
petitioner are not on record.
6

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
9. In order to resolve the controversy, the University
is required to disclose the criteria, if any, prescribed
by it for adjudging suitability of candidates during
interview and also place on record the marks obtained
by the petitioner in the interview to enable the Court
to examine whether the petitioner was entitled for
appointment against the post in question, or not.
10. List after two weeks."
12. Learned counsel for the university has filed a
supplementary affidavit disclosing the criteria adopted
for selection and has also produced the result of the
candidates who applied against the post of Assistant
Professor (Statistics) in the College of Forestry under
the EWS category. The selection criteria adopted by the
university, as disclosed in the supplementary affidavit,
reveals that a screening committee was constituted in
terms of the provisions of the Statute of the university
and the selection was made as per the provisions of the
UGC Regulation, 2018.
13. The short-listed candidates were called for
interview and presentation. Out of total 25 marks, 5
marks were provided for presentation (teaching skills
and discussion) and 20 marks for interview.
14. The petitioner obtained 2 marks in
presentation and 13 marks in interview whereas
respondent no.3 obtained 4 marks in presentation and
17 marks in interview. Thus, out of total 25 marks, the
7

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
petitioner had obtained 15 marks whereas respondent
no.3 obtained 21 marks.
15. The moot question, which falls for
consideration before the Court, is that as to whether the
candidature of respondent no.3, who never applied
under the EWS category, could have been considered
against the aforesaid post earmarked for the EWS
category.
16. The reservation to the EWS category is
governed by the Act of 2019 wherein, as per Section
2(b), "economically weaker sections" means
economically weaker sections specified in Article 15 (6)
and Article 16(6) of the Constitution.
17. Section 3 provides for reservation in favour of
economically weaker sections, Section 4 provides for the
responsibility and power for compliance of the Act,
Section 5 provides for the penalty for non-compliance of
the statutory framework under which the reservation is
provided for the EWS category, and Section 7 provides
that for claiming reservation under the Act a Certificate
is to be issued by an officer not below the rank of
Tehsildar. Section 3, 4, 5 and 7 of the Act of 2019 reads
as under:
8

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
Reservation in
favour of
economically
weaker sections
3. In public services and posts, on the order of direct
recruitment vacancies to be recruited in accordance
with the roster specified in sub-section (4), 10 percent
shall be reserved in the favour of concerned persons of
the economically weaker sections.
(a) In public services and posts, the reservation in favour of
economically weaker sections shall be given to such
permanent residents of the State of Uttarakhand, which are
not included in the existing reservations schemes for
Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Socially and
Educationally Backward Classes.
(b) The persons of such economically weaker sections are
identified for the reservation as economically weaker
section, whose gross annual income of family, from all sources
is less than 8.00 lakh (eight lakh). Family income includes
income received from all sources namely-salary, agriculture,
profession, business etc. The said income shall be income of
the previous financial year, from the year of application, by
the beneficiary ;
Provided that the person or their family possess
any property, from the following properties, shall not be
eligible for the reservation as economically weaker
sections:-
(i) 5 acre of agricultural land or above; or
(ii) residential building of 1000 sq. feet or above;
or
(iii) residential plot of 100 sq. yards or
above in notified municipalities; or
(iv) residential plot of 200 sq. yards or above in
areas other than the notified municipalities.
1[(3) If, in any recruitment year any vacancy reserved for
Economically Weaker Sections cannot be filled up due
to non availability of a suitable candidate, then such
vacancies for that particular recruitment year shall not
be carried forward to the next recruitment year as
backlog and such vacancy shall be filled up from a
suitable candidate belonging to General category.
If , any person belonging to Economically
Weaker Sections selected against the quota reserved for
persons with benchmark disabilities/ ex-servicemen then
such person shall be placed against the roster points
earmarked for Economically Weaker Sections.]
9

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
(4) The State Government shall, for applying
the
reservation under sub-section (1), by notified order
issue a roaster which shall continuously apply, till it is
exhausted.
(5) If a person belonging to economically weaker
sections as mentioned in sub-section (1), get selected
on the basis on merit in an open completion with
general candidates, he/she shall not be adjusted against
the vacancies, reserved for such category, under
sub- section (1).
Responsibility
and power for
compliance of Act
4. (1) The State Government may by notified order entrust the
appointing authority or any officer or employee with
responsibility of ensuring the compliance of the
provisions of this Act.
(2) The State Government may in the like manner west the
appointing authority or officer referred in sub section
with such power or authority as may be necessary
for effective discharging the responsibility entrusted to
him under sub section (1).
Penalty 5. (1) Any appointing authority or officer or employee
entrusted with the responsibility under sub-section (1) of
Section 4, willfully acts in manner to contravene or defeat
the purposes of this Act shall, on conviction, be
punishable with imprisonment which may extend to 3
months or with fine which may extend to 20000 or both;
(2) No court shall take the cognizance of any offence under
this section except with the previous sanction of the State
Government or an officer authorized in this behalf by
the State Government by order ;
(3) An offence punishable under sub section (1) shall be tried
summarily by a Metropolitan Magistrate or Judicial
Magistrate of First class and provision of sub section (1)
of Section 262, Section 263, Section 264 and Section 265
of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 shall mutatis
mutandis apply.
Certificate 7. For the purposes of reservation provided under this Act,
certificate of economically weaker section shall be issued
by such officer or authority and in such manner and form
as the State Government shall, by order, provide ;
Provided that certificate regarding income and
property shall be issued by officer not below the rank of
Tahsildar, following the proper procedure after carefully
verifying the all relevant rules.
18. Admittedly, respondent no.3 does not belong
to EWS category and no certificate, as required under
10

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
Section 7 of the Act, was produced by him before
respondent no.2 though time was granted to him to
produce the said certificate. Learned counsel for the
university (respondent nos.1 and 2) has fairly conceded
that the post of Assistant Professor (Statistics) under
the College of Forestry was to be filled up under the
EWS category and the advertisement enclosed with the
writ petition as Annexure No.1 also fortify the said fact.
Moreover, as per the own case of respondent no.3, he
had never applied under the EWS category, as such, the
inclusion of the name of the respondent no.3 for
selection to be made against the post earmarked for
EWS category was not proper and was against the
statutory framework of the Act of 2019.
19. As per Section 3(3) of the Act of 2019, if in
any recruitment year any vacancy reserved for EWS
cannot be filled up due to non-availability of a suitable
candidate then such vacancy for that particular
recruitment year is not to be carried forward and is to
be filled up from a suitable candidate belonging to
General Category.
20. A perusal of the record reveals that no
minimum cut-off marks were provided by the Section
Committee, as such, it cannot be said that the petitioner
11

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
could not obtain the requisite marks and was found
unsuitable. The candidature of the petitioner was
considered vis-à-vis the candidature of respondent no.3
and respondent no.3 was recommended as he obtained
more marks than the petitioner. Thus, it was not a case
where due to non-availability of a suitable EWS
candidate the respondent no.3 being a general category
candidate was considered against the EWS reserved
post. As such, the contention of the learned counsel for
respondent no.3 that the petitioner was found
unsuitable and, as such, candidature of respondent no.3
could have been considered against the EWS category
post is bereft of merit.
21. In view of the above discussion, we are of the
considered view that the selection and recommendation
of respondent no.3 against the EWS category post was
against the provisions of the Act of 2019 and was illegal.
The said recommendation being contrary to the law
cannot be sustained and is, accordingly, quashed. The
respondents are directed to consider the candidature of
the petitioner for appointment to the post of Assistant
Professor (Statistics) in the College of Forestry under the
EWS category and to issue appointment letter in favour
of petitioner within three weeks from today.
12

UKHC010042072025
2026:UHC:9009-DB
22. The writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
23. Pending application, if any, also stands
disposed of.
 (MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
